stem: When examining the tongue for possible squamous cell carcinoma, which areas are most important to inspect?

options.text: The dorsal surface and the large papillae at the back
The lateral borders and the ventral surface
The tip of the tongue and the midline
The lingual tonsils at the base of the tongue
The circumvallate papillae on the posterior dorsum

explanation: The lateral borders and ventral surface are the key areas to inspect because early oral squamous cell carcinoma commonly presents there as subtle ulcers, red patches, or white patches.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the dorsal surface is not the main site where early tongue cancers are most likely to be found.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the lateral borders and ventral surface are common sites for early oral squamous cell carcinoma and can show subtle mucosal change.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the tip and midline are less important than the lateral and inferior surfaces for detecting early lesions.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because lingual tonsils are lymphoid tissue at the tongue base, not the main focus when inspecting for tongue mucosal malignancy.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the circumvallate papillae are normal posterior dorsal structures and are not the key areas for screening for squamous cell carcinoma.

source.hint: The examiner used gauze to pull the tongue to the side to see these areas.
